This is warranted explanatory diagram scope, not a missing proof.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Path vertices indexed by integers; 2n represents r^n and 2n+1 represents r^n a, where a^2=b^2=e and r=ab.
diagram_math_checks.relations: r^n a is obtained from r^n by right a; (r^n a)b=r^(n+1). Thus the four explicit central edges, -2 to -1 to 0 to 1 to 2, have labels a,b,a,b. Each interior vertex has degree two and both ends continue.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Item F1 uses right multiplication; step 1.1 chooses the two-involution presentation and step 2.1 identifies its infinite path.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Ladder vertices (n,epsilon) represent r^n s^epsilon with s=b, s^2=e and srs=r^-1.
diagram_math_checks.relations: Right s swaps epsilon and leaves n fixed. Right r sends (n,0) to (n+1,0) and (n,1) to (n-1,1); hence undirected horizontal r edges join consecutive n in either row. The displayed finite window has six vertices, four complete horizontal edges and three rungs, plus four horizontal continuation stubs. Interior column vertices have degree three. There are no directed-edge or closing-cycle assertions.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1.1 and L8 use the inverting involution presentation and generalized dihedral product. The local def-generalized-dihedral-group inversion action and def-external-semidirect-product multiplication give (n,epsilon)(m,delta)=(n+(-1)^epsilon m,epsilon+delta mod 2). Also b(ab)b=ba=(ab)^-1.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Projection p from the infinite undirected ladder, Z times {0,1}, to the integer path, p(n,epsilon)=n.
diagram_math_checks.relations: Each edge changes n by at most one, so |p(x)-p(y)|<=d(x,y). A horizontal path and at most one rung gives d(x,y)<=|p(x)-p(y)|+1. Each two-point fibre is one rung of diameter one. For Z times C2, right multiplication by its standard generators gives the same undirected edges.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These are direct path-length checks on the graph of step 2.1 using the F1 convention and L1 word metric; they explain the existing graph comparison without altering the proof.
